correctness.rationale: For K_(n1,...,nr), r>=3, each n_i>=2, exactly two leaders and unit edges, grounded L_FF=M-11^T has invertible diagonal-plus-all-ones blocks. Sherman–Morrison gives exact inverse-trace J and the formulas for same-part and mixed-part placements. Same-part J(vv)-J(uu)=(N-4)(v-u)/[2(N-u)(N-v)] for u<=v, strict when u<v. For mixed u<=v, subtract same smaller-part objective; after h=u-2>=0, d=v-u>=0, R=N-u-v>=2, numerator has five strictly/nonnegatively coefficient polynomials, denominator positive. Independently verified that polynomial identity symbolically (SymPy), and exact matrix inverse traces for 213 pairs over 5 distinct multipartite graphs; K_(2,3,7) optimum 361/180. Thus every optimum is a same-smallest-part pair, count (#minimum parts)binom(m,2).
residual_risks: No singleton part, weighted-edge, more-than-two-leader or heterogeneous noise theorem.

value.rationale: Two perfect leaders concentrating in one smallest, mutually nonadjacent community is a non-obvious exact optimization rule in a natural heterogeneous dense-network model. It resolves every optimizer, not a case study or trivial parameter substitution, and supplies the exact performance and multiplicity useful for network design.
residual_risks: The assumption of identical follower noise and unit cross-part conductances is important to real-world applicability.

limitations: No result for singleton parts, higher budgets, noisy leaders, or heterogeneous conductances.
Global optimality depends on proving both same-part and mixed-part inequalities, not on finite search.
